criteria.criterion: A test with the fake agent exceeds a short producer deadline after editing files. Afterwards the edits remain in the job worktree, a progress note listing the changed files exists, and the job is recorded as timed out, not failed. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: I ran a_producer_that_hits_its_deadline_keeps_its_work_and_closes_timed_out and it passed. The test has the fake producer edit src/partial.rs and README.md and end TimedOut with 'deadline of 1800s reached'. It then checks four things. outcome.json has state TimedOut. The 02-producer invocation is TimedOut. The committed progress-note.md names both files. <state>/repo/kept/<job>/work still holds both edited files. Without the change, run.rs would send TimedOut down the old non-Success path, close the job Failed, and delete the work tree in clean_job.

criteria.criterion: A test retries a timed-out job. The new producer starts from the kept worktree (not a clean checkout) and is given the progress note naming the earlier changed files. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: I ran retrying_a_timed_out_job_starts_from_the_kept_work_with_the_note and it passed. Inside the second producer call, the test checks that src/partial.rs already exists in spec.workdir, and that the brief has '## Resume' and names both files. It also checks that the new job id differs and that the kept directory is gone once the retry closes. retrying_a_timed_out_job_whose_base_moved_starts_clean also passed: when the base has moved, the retry starts with no kept file and no Resume section. The unit test a_resume_brief_carries_the_progress_note passed as well.

criteria.criterion: Status output distinguishes a timed-out job from a failed one, and the deadline reason (e.g. 'deadline of 1800s reached') is kept in the record. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: I ran status_shows_timed_out_apart_from_failed and it passed. The test closes one job TimedOut and one Failed (a Killed producer). It asserts that status.recent shows 'timed_out' and 'failed' and that jobs_by_state has timed_out=1. The state strings come from OutcomeState::as_str through JobState::name (store.rs:69), and that is the text status prints. The criterion-1 test checks that both the outcome reason and the invocation detail contain 'deadline of 1800s reached'.

criteria.criterion: A test shows existing records with killed or failed outcomes still deserialize unchanged, and a job that finishes in time behaves as before. Run: cargo test.
criteria.evidence: I ran three tests and all passed. records::tests::old_killed_and_failed_outcomes_still_deserialize parses the literal "killed" and "failed" values and round-trips timed_out. a_killed_invocation_is_recorded_with_bounds is unchanged. a_killed_producer_keeps_nothing_and_a_job_in_time_leaves_no_note shows a Killed producer still closes Failed with no note and no kept directory, and a normal job still lands with no kept directory. Athena's full cargo test record also passed, which includes the existing happy-path tests.

criteria.criterion: The new timed-out outcome is documented and CHANGELOG.md mentions the change.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: OutcomeState::TimedOut and InvocationOutcome::TimedOut have rustdoc. docs/records.md adds timed_out to the outcome states and a paragraph on the kept work, progress-note.md and the Resume section. The CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Added entry covers the timed-out outcome, the kept work, the progress note, the retry resume, the status display, drain, readability of old records, and the producer-only scope. I checked these claims against run.rs, state.rs, briefs.rs and drain.rs and they match.

findings.summary: Kept work of a timed-out job that is never retried is never cleaned up
findings.evidence: remove_kept_work runs only when a retry that resumed from the kept work closes. A timed-out job that is closed or abandoned without a retry leaves <state>/kept/<job>/work on disk indefinitely.

summary: The change passes: all six criteria are met and there are no blocker or major findings. When the producer hits its deadline, the invocation is now recorded as timed out and the job closes as timed out instead of failed. The work tree is moved to <state>/kept/<job>/work, and a progress note listing the changed files is committed with the job's records. `athena retry` starts the next producer from a copy of that work, and the producer's brief gets a 'Resume' section quoting the note. If the base has changed or the job was a pinned study, the retry starts clean as before. Status and drain treat timed out as its own state. Old killed and failed records still read unchanged. I ran the new tests myself: four in lifecycle, one in drain, the brief and records unit tests, and the existing killed-producer tests. All passed. Athena's fmt, clippy and test records for this tree also passed. There are three minor findings. The change touches more files than the expected deliverables list, though most were in the accepted plan. invocation.rs is on the list but was not changed. Kept work for a timed-out job that is never retried is never deleted.
